name: Google Maps ranking service for local businesses (white-label)
one_liner: Sell Google Business Profile ranking audits and ongoing Maps optimisation to local service businesses, using white-labelled software and finding clients through cheap Facebook ads that book calls.
customer: Local business owners, especially higher-ticket service businesses that depend on Google Maps leads
offer: Monthly Google Maps ranking and optimisation service. A free ranking audit call is the way in. Review and reputation management can be added later.
how_it_makes_money: Monthly retainer. The host suggests charging $400–600/month per client against roughly $100/month per client for the white-label software.
startup_cost: low; about $30/day in Facebook ads plus about $100/month per client for software
time_to_first_revenue: About 1 month: first deal closed, 3 active clients after a month starting from zero
evidence: The founder had a customer-service career in England and no experience; 3 active clients after a month (RWmEE6ra--g)
Calls booked at about $30 each, falling to about $18 once the ads were reworded around 'rank higher on Google Maps' (RWmEE6ra--g)
Software 'maybe a hundred bucks a client', 'should be able to sell it between like four and 600' (RWmEE6ra--g)
Prospects cared about ranking more than review management (RWmEE6ra--g)
risks: Needs sales calls, so it is not very async
A crowded local SEO market with churn risk
Results depend on the software and can take time to show
The pricing is the host's estimate, not the founder's actual pricing

customer: Startup founders, marketers and site owners who need specific automations (for example, SEO content)
offer: Small SaaS tools and AI agents, such as an automated SEO content bot
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; the founder runs tools internally for 1–3 years before launching

'Little tools ... You can build them in one evening' (SiRlIMtZygI)

A long incubation before launch

name: Custom dashboard and internal-tool agency built with AI app builders
one_liner: Use Bolt or similar AI builders to build custom dashboards and copies of SaaS tools for small businesses, charging agency prices for very low build costs.
customer: Small and medium businesses that pay for SaaS subscriptions or need reporting dashboards
offer: Custom dashboards, internal tools and web apps with built-in payments
how_it_makes_money: Project fees per build (one example was $9,000) plus optional maintenance retainers
startup_cost: low; about $9 in Bolt usage for the cited build
time_to_first_revenue: unknown; builds take minutes to days, but you still have to find clients
evidence: CJ: 'it cost me nine bucks on Bolt' and charged the client $9,000 (VmROvPvi_iM)
'People will pay so much money for a dashboard. Go start a dang dashboard agency' (VmROvPvi_iM)

Clients may need ongoing support and security work

name: Branded commodity product sold direct-to-consumer with AI-made ads
one_liner: Repackage a cheap commodity (sugar sold as 'hummingbird nectar mix') under a brand, and sell it through an AI-built store and Meta ads.
customer: Hobby consumers who buy something repeatedly (bird feeders in the example)
offer: Branded, heat-sealed pouches of a commodity mix
how_it_makes_money: Product margin at $14 per bag, against bulk sugar costing $39.97 per 50 lb, with repeat purchases
startup_cost: low; a $20 heat sealer, bulk sugar, a Solo Drop store and an ad budget (testing at about $100/day)
time_to_first_revenue: Launched overnight; the store took about 12 minutes to build
tools: Meta Ads (ABO testing and scaling campaigns)
evidence: An Amazon listing with 24,000 reviews; '80,000 people have bought this more than once'; about $11 for 64 oz (UcFBcfrmC2k)
Estimated $20–30M of sugar water sold on Amazon (UcFBcfrmC2k)
hummingbirdfood.co launched at $14 with all-AI creatives (UcFBcfrmC2k)
risks: There are no hummingbirds in the UK, so it would need a different UK product (for example, wild-bird food or a hobby consumable)
Profit depends on ad costs and on shipping heavy goods
The host's own sales results weren't shown
Food and animal-product labelling rules

name: Washer/dryer rental through Facebook Marketplace
one_liner: Buy cheap used washers and dryers and rent them monthly to local tenants through Facebook Marketplace listings.
customer: Renters and households without laundry machines
how_it_makes_money: Recurring monthly rent per unit. Units cost about $50 each. Pre-renting before buying recovers the purchase cost.
startup_cost: low; can start at about $0 by renting units out before buying them, and units cost about $50
time_to_first_revenue: Fast; units are rented out before the money is spent
tools: ChatGPT for picking what to rent
evidence: A 23-year-old makes $10,000/month with no employees, working 5 hours a week (UCdWRg1KQLY)
Units cost about $50; 'start this business with literally zero dollars? Yes' (UCdWRg1KQLY)
Earlier micro-rentals included paddle boards and a game rented for a couple of hundred dollars a month (UCdWRg1KQLY)
risks: Delivery, installation and repairs must be done in person
UK flats often come with appliances already
Damage and non-payment
Facebook may ban listings

how_it_makes_money: Rental fees: $300 for 2 hours, $450 for 4 hours, $525 for 8 hours, $600 overnight, plus $200 for a weekend
startup_cost: medium-high; trailer units (the cost wasn't stated in the excerpt)
time_to_first_revenue: Some operators break even in about 75 days
evidence: Operators make $10–50k/month at about 50% gross margin (VGAOCH2vYwM)
Search volume for these keywords rose 370%; the cold plunge market was $318M, projected to reach about $500M by 2030 (VGAOCH2vYwM)
10 rentals a month at an average of $450 gives $4,500/month (VGAOCH2vYwM)

name: Subscription neighbourhood trash collection
one_liner: Win a neighbourhood fed up with a failing waste hauler, using a pre-sold, money-back offer, then finance discounted trucks.
how_it_makes_money: $35–60 per house per month. 400 houses is about $12k/month. The business does $50k/month at about 40% gross margin.
startup_cost: high; trucks bought with close to 100% financing at about a 70% discount
evidence: $50,000/month; 'we've never had a customer cancelled' (UgFzXqa7zNM)
